text:
Ben H.: heads up — saw a burst of GPU pod evictions in us-west2 last night around 22:13 UTC, looks correlated with an autoscaler ramp + egress saturation :thinking_face:
Ben H.: sample from controller logs:
```
I0320 22:13:27 eviction_controller.go:142] evicting pod gpu-train-42 on node gnode-45 reason=NetworkUnavailable
W0320 22:13:28 kubelet.go:210] network plugin reported high outstanding flows, marking NotReady
```
Ben H.: a lot of tiny pods (0.25-0.5 GPU) got preempted, then larger training pods couldn't binpack and stayed pending — fragmentation spike
Alice M.: :eyes: do we have node-level metrics for conntrack / ENI usage at that window? can we rule out cloud network throttling?
Darren: checking cloud console now — there's a concurrent benign scale event for web-tier that increased egress by ~600Mbps for a short burst, might have pushed CNI rules over conntrack limits
Cara: that matches — we've seen conntrack overflow => kubelet marks node network unhealthy => eviction cascade. small pods exacerbate it because scheduler spreads them across nodes
Ryan: what about warm-pool placement? are tiny pods landing on warm nodes or cold new nodes? warm nodes are more fragmented
Ben H.: warm nodes mostly, but autoscaler pressure forced cold racks to spin up too; cold nodes had different taints so tiny pods landed sparse, causing fragmentation
Cara: we should try a two-pronged fix: 1) conntrack tuning + egress shaping, 2) packing tiny GPU pods together via topologySpread / podAffinity or a scheduler plugin
Ryan: agree. also can we throttle web-tier burst or move to egress-limited AZs during rolling deploys as a patch
Darren: quick mitigation I spun up: bumped node conntrack sysctl on GPU nodes and added a short-lived descheduler job to coalesce small pods onto fewer nodes
Darren: descheduler job snippet I used:
```
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata: {name: "coalesce-tiny-gpus"}
spec: {template:{spec:{containers:[{name:"ds", image:"descheduler:v1", args:["--strategy=RemoveDuplicates"]}], restartPolicy:"Never"}}}
```
Ben H.: nice. early results look promising — eviction rate dropped to near zero after descheduler completed and conntrack bump applied
Alice M.: follow-up items: run a 24h conntrack stress test in us-west2, add autoscaler deploy cool-down to avoid coincident egress surges, and add a packing policy for fractional GPU workloads
Cara: can we add a scheduler predicate to prefer packing fractional GPUs onto nodes with matching tiny-pod labels? maybe a fastbeta feature flag
Ryan: I'll prototype a plugin that prefers label `gpu-slot=compact` and we can label a subset of warm nodes, then rollout via feature flag
sched-bot: scheduled job: run conntrack-stress-us-west2 at 2026-03-22T02:00:00Z (CI)
ops-bot: created ticket INF-4821: "us-west2 conntrack evict cascade — mitigation + packing policy" and assigned to @Ryan and @Cara
Ben H.: cool, one more note — cost side: fragmentation increased committed GPU hours by ~8% during the event. include that in INF-4821
Cara: noted. I'll add a short eval to Redwood Optimize to simulate packing gains for fractional pods
Ben H.: thanks everyone. will follow up with postmortem if stress test reproduces the cascade :thumbsup:
